nodes.title: A serious finding (🔴/🟠) goes to a fresh agent that did not find it and tries to refute it, re-reading every quoted line and running the check again, before the author fixes it: a confirmed one is fixed; a refuted one is recorded as rejected with why; one whose deciding fact is out of reach is needs-validation, with that exact fact, no severity, and a graph node. Convergence counts the refuted ones, so fixes of findings that were not real are measured; the refuter never takes a lack of disproof as confirmation, and names the precondition the defect needs (Compound Engineering's ce-code-review validator; OpenAI's code reviewer chose fewer, checked findings over recall)
nodes.source: review of cloudflare/security-audit-skill (MIT, c1c8a8c), 2026-10-25: 'the agent that checks a finding is never the agent that found it'; three verdicts: confirmed, needs_validation (an exact unresolved fact, no severity) and rejected. Ennyn's evidence: fixes introduced more defects than first drafts missed (99 against 80 in the origin project; in Ennyn's cycles 2-10, 245 fix-introduced against 266 real escapes), and fixing a finding that was not real is pure risk
